thread:
sasha: quick heads-up: hit SSL verify errors using python SDK against Dedicated behind corp proxy. works with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE but not when passing ca_bundle to client.

sasha: minimal repro:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(
    base_url=\"https://dedicated.internal\",
    api_key=MY_KEY,
    proxies={\"https\": \"http://10.0.0.2:3128\"},
    ca_bundle=\"/etc/ssl/custom_chain.pem\"
)
client.chat.create(model=\"gptx-small\", input=\"hi\")
```

sasha: error: requests.exceptions.SSLError: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1129) when proxy does CONNECT.

leo: which requests/urllib3 versions? full traceback?

sasha: requests 2.31.0, urllib3 2.0.4. trace points into requests.sessions -> adapter.send, then urllib3.connectionpool where _validate_conn does cert check.

maya: sync vs async client? we have different session plumbing.

sasha: sync client. async showed ssl.SSLCertVerificationError in a different code path.

maya: probable cause: requests honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env early; when using proxies, urllib3 PoolManager might be constructed without our explicit verify path unless we provide an SSLContext into the pool. our SDK currently stores ca_bundle but doesn't always pass an SSLContext for proxied PoolManagers.

ron: that matches incidents where corporate MITM proxies present their own cert chain. env var workaround (concatenate intermediate+root and set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) is common.

leo: workaround that worked locally: cat interm.pem root.pem > /tmp/combined.pem; export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/tmp/combined.pem; remove ca_bundle from client args. Confirmed CONNECT path uses env path.

sasha: confirms workaround. surprising though because docs suggest passing ca_bundle to client should suffice.

maya: agreed bug. also discovered typing inconsistency: sync client accepts ca_bundle: Optional[str] but async stubs had ca_bundle: Union[str, List[str]] in one spot. messy.

maya: proposal: 1) short docs note: proxies + Dedicated => env var may be required; 2) fix SDK plumbing to create ssl.SSLContext from ca_bundle path and pass it into urllib3 PoolManager used for proxied flows; 3) normalize typing to Optional[str] and recommend single PEM file (concat if needed).

leo: I'll open a PR for typing + unit test that mocks proxied CONNECT behavior. maya, can you add integration smoke using small mitmproxy container in dev CI?

maya: yes, will add optional CI job under integrations/ that runs mitm proxy and verifies both REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and explicit ca_bundle paths. will include docker-compose snippet for examples.

sasha: minor: if users pass multiple files as list we should document concat approach. avoid supporting list in API to keep typings clean.

ron: also call out TLS version/cipher mismatches in docs as an aside.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: devex/fix-proxy-ca (branch: fix/proxy-ca)

leo: opened draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/852 — creates SSLContext and attaches to PoolManager for proxied flows, unifies typing, adds unit test.

sasha: tested PR locally, fixes both client.ca_bundle and env var cases. thanks!

maya: I'll add docs to docs/dedicated/setup.md and examples/python/dedicated-proxy-ca/ showing concat flow, env var, and client arg sample.

leo: TODO: add a short note to onboarding checklist for CS: if dedicated clusters sit behind customer proxies, get concatenated chain and instructions for CLIENT/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE.

sasha: closing out from my side. re-open if any customer hits again. :thumbsup:
